name: warren-dogfood-http-dispatch
description: Operating warren-on-warren dogfood loops via app.warren.run HTTP API: dispatch with POST /runs {agent:'pi', modelOverride:'claude-opus-4-8', project, ref:'k8s-migration', seedId, prompt} using WARREN_API_TOKEN from .env.deployed; plan-runs via POST /plan-runs {planId} correctly skip closed children (resume). Under maxed GKE quota, parallel dispatches are all admitted (no 429) and serialize to one pod; queued runs drain in order. PRs automerge via the auto-merge workflow unless an Article IX protected path (.canopy/, docs/CONSTITUTION.md, triggers.yaml, auto-merge.yml) is in the diff — remediation is reverting the protected file on the PR branch (commit --no-verify, push), which re-triggers enablement. Watch runs with a state-transition poller that reports pr_open stalls, not just terminal states.

title: Warren's plot/canopy/conversation bundling is retired (pl-3a79 landed)
rationale: The pl-3a79 deletion pass removed conversations, plot (with its plan-run bridges), and canopy (both the library tier and the project tier) from warren's code, DB, UI, config, CLI, and env surface. Warren now integrates only mulch, seeds, and sapling as opt-in features plus the inline built-in agents; plan-run is a dispatch mode over the single-run primitive, not a bundled feature. Plot and canopy live on as independent os-eco tools — only warren's bundling of them was removed. Prior warren-integration expertise for these three tools (the plots domain, canopy library/project-tier records, conversation records) is obsolete and kept for traceability, mirroring the greenhouse precedent.

description: Deployed-instance drift is a live failure class: app.warren.run (v0.12.2) seeded .canopy/agent.json into run workspaces and its pi builtin's system prompt pointed agents at that path, weeks after main relocated the drop to .warren/agent.json (3ca5d514, warren-5585). Unreleased main fixes do not exist for the live instance — dogfood runs execute against the last deployed image, so every dispatched run re-observes already-fixed bugs. Detection: compare GET /version against the fix's release tag before diagnosing 'regressions' seen in run events. Filed warren-1899; resolution is releasing+deploying 0.13.0.
resolution: Filed warren-1899; cut 0.13.0 and deploy; consider reap-time seed-reset dropping stray .canopy/agent.json as defense-in-depth

name: warren-dogfood-p1-pipeline-2026-08
description: Warren dogfood P1 pipeline (2026-07-31/08-01): 8 P1 issues dispatched sequentially to app.warren.run on pi + openrouter/moonshotai/kimi-k3; 8/8 runs succeeded, 8/8 PRs (#709-#716) merged, 2 conflict-repair runs (both .seeds/budget overlaps, both healed by repair-run-on-PR-branch with targetBranch pinned), total agent spend ~$4.71. Working patterns: (1) embed live-instance evidence digests in investigation-run prompts — the sandboxed agent cannot query the API; the warren-3047 run root-caused finalize loss (blind pod-log follow + 300s finalize give-up) from the embedded event timeline alone and filed warren-029d/warren-4d6a; (2) when an issue is re-scoped locally mid-session, the dispatch prompt must carry the authoritative spec AND have the agent sd update the tracker first — agent clones read origin, not the operator's working tree; (3) split live-DB actions out of dispatch prompts (ef12: operator ran the 48,707-row Supabase purge; agent shipped only the bridge filter).

warren K8s dogfood dispatch (pi + kimi-k3, plan-run pl-2dbb child 1): run hung after agent settled — stdin-hold watchdog killed pi without a terminal envelope, reap never triggered, pod polled finalize-intent forever, run row stuck running. Salvage captured nothing (no git credential in window; agent had not committed). Manual recovery: kubectl exec into live pod, git add/commit with pod's GIT_AUTHOR_* env, git bundle main..HEAD, kubectl cp out, fetch bundle into local repo, push branch, hand-open PR. Root cause + fix sketch recorded in warren-9a4a; salvage gaps in warren-6016.
resolution: Until warren-9a4a ships: do not dispatch stdin-held (pi) agents to the K8s instance for unattended runs; claude-code batch agent is immune (emits result envelope). If a run hangs at settle: salvage via kubectl exec commit + bundle BEFORE cancelling (cancel deletes the pod and the emptyDir).

description: Plan-run seeds conflicts are structural, not incidental: closing any plan child rewrites updatedAt+blockedBy on the parent and all siblings, so every pair of consecutive sibling PRs conflicts on .seeds/issues.jsonl. The seeds-jsonl driver set-merges blockedBy fine but fails on both-changed updatedAt scalars. Manual fix that works: normalize updatedAt to max(ours,theirs) on the conflicted rows in both stage files, re-run 'bun scripts/merge-seeds-jsonl.ts anc ours theirs', verify check:seeds-integrity + no dup ids, push. Filed warren-d8f0 to make the driver do this itself.
resolution: Normalize both-changed updatedAt to max then re-run driver; filed warren-d8f0 for the permanent fix

name: extension-deps-ci-install
description: First extension with a real npm dependency (@warren-ext/judge -> @sinclair/typebox) broke root bun test in CI: the root sweep discovers extensions/*/src/*.test.ts but CI only ran root bun install, so extension node_modules never existed (audit-log masked this with zero deps). Fix pattern mirrors ui:install: root script ext:install = 'for d in extensions/*/; do (cd $d && bun install); done' + a CI step before the test sweep, and the same step in release.yml. A warren repair run (ref=targetBranch=PR head branch) shipped it for $0.30.

description: Warren dogfood pipeline session 2026-08-15: plan pl-17ca (judge-layer extension, 8 children) ran end-to-end through app.warren.run on pi + openrouter/moonshotai-kimi-k3 — 8 issue runs + 1 repair run, PRs #876-#883 all auto-merged, total agent spend $8.35, wall-clock ~3h. description: good-first-issue batch 2026-08-18: warren-a553 (transient provider_error auto-retry) was born dead — PR #935/191c0ef1 (warren-339d) shipped the exact run-level retry ~19.5h before the row was filed, because the author observed a live instance running an older deploy. Second confirmed instance of the born-dead pattern (#808 was the first).
resolution: Verification against HEAD before filing caught it: closed warren-a553 citing 191c0ef1, split the live residual (retry classifier ignores structured httpStatus from warren-4001 enrichment) into warren-f8b2 and filed it as GitHub #975. Rows filed from live-instance observations need a deployed-version-vs-HEAD check on top of the standard born-dead git-log check.
